title: A sequential-access KSDS: REWRITE with no READ before it ends in file status 43, and REWRITE that gives a unique alternate key a duplicate value ends in 22
shapes: AIXA AIXAKS3: SELECT CUS-FILE ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL with ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS CUS-TAX (no DUPLICATES) and CUS-NAME WITH DUPLICATES; 0000-MAIN OPEN I-O, PERFORMs 1000-BLIND (REWRITE straight after OPEN, tests '43') then 2000-CLASH (READ NEXT, MOVE a TAX ID another record holds to CUS-TAX, REWRITE, tests '22')
AIXA jcl/AIXARU2.jcl KS3040: //CUSKSD, //CUSKSD1 (TAX path) and //CUSKSD2 (NAME path) on the same clusters as KS2030
asserts: The SELECT is one file_control fact (select CUS-FILE, assign CUSKSD, organization INDEXED, access_mode SEQUENTIAL, record_key CUS-ID) with alternate_keys [{name CUS-TAX, duplicates false}, {name CUS-NAME, duplicates true}]. 1000-BLIND and 2000-CLASH are each one units fact, PERFORMed once from 0000-MAIN as plain edges facts, and each tests the FILE STATUS item named in the SELECT (WS-CUS-STATUS). At run time, REWRITE of an indexed file in sequential access mode when the last I-O statement was not a successfully executed READ ends in 43 (high-order digit 4, logic error); REWRITE of a record after a successful READ NEXT, with CUS-TAX changed to a value another record already holds, ends in 22 (digit 2, invalid key) because CUS-TAX has no DUPLICATES phrase. CUS-NAME WITH DUPLICATES would not raise 22 for the same change. Step KS3040 has four jcl_dds facts: STEPLIB, CUSKSD, CUSKSD1, CUSKSD2, the latter two naming the paths.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: For relative and indexed files in the sequential access mode, the last input-output statement executed for the file prior to the execution of a DELETE or REWRITE statement was not a successfully executed READ statement.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Or an attempt was made to write or rewrite a record that would create a duplicate prime record key or a duplicate alternate record key without the DUPLICATES phrase in an indexed file.

notes: Quotes are the Table 34 entries for 43 and 22 from igy6lr40.pdf via pdftotext, joined across line breaks. The 22 quote starts mid-sentence because Table 34 continues the entry for relative files. The 22 outcome assumes the data set holds a record with tax id 987654321 other than the one read (AIXAKS2 writes one); no step orders the two programs' data beyond that and the statuses are what IBM says for such a data set. Changing the prime key on REWRITE is a different case, not planted. GnuCOBOL statuses were not compared.
